summary: International-break Friday: 16 candidates, all in well-covered competitions (Nations League, WTA Finals, EuroLeague, CS2). The 8 best-covered were researched first and 7 are kept at medium confidence and Panathinaikos over Barcelona at low (only three sources, no second price or model; Barcelona without Punter and Evbuomwan); the other 8 (smaller Nations League games, CS2, two EuroLeague games) were not reached. Medium: Scotland over North Macedonia (North Macedonia scoreless in 8; Scotland need the win; p 0.81), Germany in Serbia (Serbia without Vlahovic, Pavlovic, Kostic and Stankovic, near-empty stadium; Germany blunt under Klopp; p 0.75), Slovakia over Faroe Islands (Lobotka, Dubravka out; Faroes drew all four group games; p 0.70), Andreeva over Muchová (Andreeva qualified, Muchová out; dead rubber; Elo below the market; p 0.68), Sabalenka over Svitolina (winner takes the last semi-final place; h2h 6-1; p 0.67), Netherlands v Greece (Van Dijk and Brobbey out; Greece under 1.5 goals at 0.73) and Slovenia v Switzerland (a point promotes Switzerland; Slovenia +1.5 at 0.71). No high: lineups not out yet; the pre-kickoff check re-checks the slip about 100 minutes before its first game. No Stake or Rainbet prices were found; DraftKings prices via ESPN were used for every football game. Pre-kickoff check (about 18:10 UTC): Scotland, Slovenia–Switzerland, Serbia–Germany, Slovakia and Andreeva re-checked with live prices. There is no late injury, illness or withdrawal news, and no price has moved against any favourite (Germany and Slovakia shortened). No official XI or order of play was out yet, so all stay medium. At live prices the best slip moves from North Macedonia under 0.5 goals to Slovakia under 2.5 team goals, still with Switzerland draw no bet.

checks.team_news: Re-checked at about 95 min before kick-off. No new injury or illness news today. Previews still say McTominay returns, fully fit after the minor heart procedure (Goal.com), and McKenna is out. Welsh is a doubt or out. Luis Binks: some reports say he withdrew, others still name him in the XI, so this is unresolved. North Macedonia: still no injuries reported, and Miovski left out by choice. Nothing late that hurts Scotland.
checks.lineups: Official XIs are NOT out yet. The ESPN summary roster for event 401861161 is empty, and the press I found is all predicted lineups. The most common Scotland XI: Gunn; Hickey, Hendry, Binks; Gannon-Doak, McGinn, Ferguson, Gilmour, Robertson; McTominay; McBurnie. TNT instead had Porteous in the back three and Christie in support. Sources disagree on a few Scotland names, and WhoScored has a 3-5-1-1. North Macedonia expected: Dimitrievski in goal; Bardhi, Elmas and Rastoder in attack; the defence and midfield names vary by source. The starting keepers are expected to be Gunn and Dimitrievski, unconfirmed.
checks.rotation: Switzerland away follows on Mon 16 Nov, so some rotation is possible. Press previews predict a strong side with no heavy rotation, and nothing is confirmed.
checks.motivation: Unchanged. Scotland are third on 4 points in League B Group 1 and must win to avoid the drop risk. North Macedonia are bottom on 0 points with a goal difference of -10.
checks.form: Unchanged. North Macedonia have lost 5 in a row, are winless in 12 and have scored in none of their last 8. Scotland have scored only 3 goals in 4 Nations League games and lost both Hampden games under Pocognoli.
checks.h2h: Unchanged. Scotland lead 3 wins, 1 draw, 1 loss, including the 2-0 win in Skopje on 3 Oct 2026 with 25 shots to 9.
checks.odds: Live data (fetched 18:06 UTC): DraftKings Scotland 1.17, draw 6.5, North Macedonia 14, opening 1.20/5.5/11, de-vigged 0.792/0.142/0.066. Correction to the morning note: Scotland's price has shortened from 1.20 to 1.17, though the draw and North Macedonia prices have lengthened. Polymarket live home 0.826, draw 0.127, away 0.046. The 24h move on home is 0.825 to 0.825, so nothing has moved against Scotland today. The data shows a total line of 3.5, where the morning note said 2.5. Live leg prices: tt_away_0.5_under 0.595, btts_no 0.625, ou_3.5_under 0.625, ou_1.5_over 0.825.
checks.models: World Football Elo: Scotland 1718, North Macedonia 1533, expected score for Scotland 0.838, which is consistent with the market and unchanged.
checks.venue_weather: Hampden Park, 19:45 kick-off, normal home venue. No pitch or weather problems found. I did not check a forecast.

games.reason: Nothing new today hurts Scotland. The price is stable, with the book (0.792 de-vigged), Polymarket (0.826) and Elo (0.838) agreeing. McTominay is reported fit. North Macedonia have lost 5 in a row and scored in none of their last 8. Confidence stays medium because the official XIs are not out, Binks is unresolved, Scotland's own attack is poor (3 goals in 4 league games), and they lost both Hampden games under Pocognoli. The North Macedonia under 0.5 leg is about 0.62 by my view against a market of 0.595. It is a clean-sheet leg, supported by North Macedonia scoring in none of their last 8 and Scotland's solid defence. It still carries risk from a weak Scotland attack and an unknown XI.
games.main_risk: A draw or a narrow 1-0 or 0-0. Scotland's attack is blunt, and rotation ahead of Switzerland is possible. For the North Macedonia under 0.5 leg, one set-piece or counter goal from a side that has still not scored in 8 matches would sink it.

checks.team_news: Eurohoops Round 11 injury report (published 10 Nov 2026): Panathinaikos had sent no injury report; only listed absence is Nikos Rogkavopoulos (out since Round 5). Barcelona had also sent no report, but Eurohoops lists Kevin Punter (left ankle sprain, 3 to 6 weeks, will miss the Athens trip per Eurohoops 9 Nov), Tosan Evbuomwan (torn oblique, about 3 weeks), Yoan Makoundou (knee, has not played this season), and Umoja Gibson and Juan Nunez (both last played in Round 8, so apparently absent). No official late Panathinaikos update found; Greek press and Gazzetta.gr/Mundo Deportivo/Sport searches returned nothing current for this game. Rotowire euro pages returned were from other seasons and unusable.
checks.lineups: Not available: no predicted or confirmed starting fives found for either side from any source. Pre-kickoff check should confirm Panathinaikos' starters (Nunn, Lessort, Francisco, Hernangomez were prominent in recent wins).
checks.rotation: No double-round issue: Eurohoops shows both teams play on Friday 13 Nov (Panathinaikos v Barcelona, 20:15 CET at OAKA/Telekom Center Athens); neither played Wednesday or Thursday. Panathinaikos last played a EuroLeague game at Real Madrid on 4 Nov (115-112 OT win, Nunn 33 pts), about 9 days rest from a long OT game. Barcelona's last game was an ACB game at Breogan around 8 Nov (Punter hurt there), a travel and rotation spot for Barcelona's short bench. Next games: Barcelona has home games v Crvena Zvezda and Fenerbahce, then Real Madrid on 3 Dec; no sign Panathinaikos rests anyone.
checks.motivation: Panathinaikos lead the EuroLeague (8-2 in 10 games per TNT Sports table), at home, with both teams in the top 4: Barcelona 4th at 7-3. Both have a real stake in top-4 seeding; no rotation motive.
checks.form: Panathinaikos 8-2, won at Real Madrid 115-112 OT on 4 Nov and also a road win at Paris (101-95) earlier; one search snippet suggested a recent two-game losing streak earlier in the season, which was snapped. Barcelona 7-3 and on a 7-game winning streak (Eurohoops, 9 Nov), though that streak includes ACB games and they are now missing guards (Punter, Gibson, Nunez).
checks.h2h: Last season's meetings: Barcelona won 103-96 at Athens and 82-73 at home per Greek press snippets; a EuroLeague game-facts page notes Barcelona won 8 of the last 10 head-to-head meetings (older data, not verified for date). Style matchup history is unfavourable to Panathinaikos, which is the main reason p is cut below market.
checks.odds: No external bookmaker price found for this game (candidates file has no data.odds; searches returned only older seasons). Polymarket 24h move: Panathinaikos 0.80 to 0.815 (+1.9% relative), mild move in favour of the favourite. No Stake or Rainbet price seen. Market-only price, so confidence is capped at medium.
checks.models: No bookmaker-free power rating or model prediction found for this game. Only table evidence: Panathinaikos 8-2 (1st) v Barcelona 7-3 (4th) per TNT Sports; point differentials not available from a reliable source.
checks.venue_weather: Home game at Telekom Center Athens (OAKA), indoor; standard venue, no neutral-site or weather issue. Tip-off 19:15 UTC (20:15 CET).

games.reason: Set to low on review: only three source sites, no bookmaker price besides Polymarket, no rating model and no starting fives were found. Fixture verified (Eurohoops Round 11 schedule, Friday 13 Nov). Panathinaikos are table leaders at home v a Barcelona side without Punter, Evbuomwan, Makoundou and probably Gibson and Nunez, so a home win is likely and the market 0.815 is reasonable; p is trimmed to 0.80 because of Barcelona's recent head-to-head record against Panathinaikos, 7-game winning run and the lack of any odds cross-check, lineup or Panathinaikos injury confirmation.
games.main_risk: Barcelona have beaten Panathinaikos repeatedly in recent seasons (including a road win in Athens) and a short-handed Barcelona backcourt can still upset; Panathinaikos' own injury status is unconfirmed (no club report found), and no independent odds or rating source was found to validate 0.815.

checks.team_news: Germany (coach Jurgen Klopp): 24-man squad; Waldemar Anton out with muscular problems (Baku called up); the squad is young and experimental (Gruda, Karl, Jeltsch, Mohya). Serbia (coach Veljko Paunovic): without Vlahovic, Strahinja Pavlovic, Kostic, and Stankovic (adductor, left camp 9 Nov); Serbia have lost all 4 Nations League games and face relegation. Nothing new found today: no late injury, illness or withdrawal reports for either side in today's press.
checks.lineups: No official XIs yet (ESPN summary roster is empty at about 18:10 UTC; kick-off 19:45 UTC). Latest expected Germany XI (ran/other German press, 13 Nov): 4-3-3, ter Stegen; Treu, Tah, Schlotterbeck, Brown; Kimmich, Pavlovic, Wirtz; Gruda, Havertz, Scherhant, with only the right wing (Karl vs Gruda) and the full-backs (Brown/Mittelstaedt) still open. This is closer to the strongest side than the morning's conflicting predictions. Serbia expected near full strength available: Milinkovic-Savic in goal, Tadic and Jovic up front. Still unconfirmed.
checks.rotation: No heavy rotation confirmed. Predicted XI keeps the core (ter Stegen, Tah, Schlotterbeck, Kimmich, Wirtz, Havertz). Next match is the Netherlands in Berlin, but Klopp needs the win, so a strong side is likely.
checks.motivation: Group A2: Greece and Netherlands 8 points, Germany 5, Serbia 0. Germany need a win to keep the group decider in their own hands; Serbia must win to avoid relegation. Both highly motivated. Spectator ban (about 5,000 incl. children and about 50 DFB fans) reduces home advantage.
checks.form: Germany: 1W 2D 1L in the Nations League under Klopp, with a 0-0 in Greece last time (blunt attack). Serbia: 4 straight Nations League defeats, including 0-2 in Munich on 1 Oct.
checks.h2h: Germany won 2-0 in Munich on 1 Oct 2026 (Bischof, Wirtz). The most likely way the favourite fails is a draw.
checks.odds: DraftKings via ESPN now: Serbia 9.5, Draw 6.0, Germany 1.22 (opening 7.5/5.5/1.27), de-vigged 9.7/15.3/75.1, total line 3.5. Polymarket live: Germany 78.64%, draw 13.71%, Serbia 7.65%, up from 76.65% this morning (move_24h 0.775 to 0.785, +1.3% relative). The move is in Germany's favour and the DraftKings price has also shortened (1.26 to 1.22), so the sources agree at about 75-79%.
checks.models: World Football Elo: Germany 1895 vs Serbia 1683, expected score for Serbia 0.344. This supports a clear Germany favourite, though less strongly than the market.
checks.venue_weather: Rajko Mitic Stadium, Belgrade, 20:45 local. Referee Javier Alberola Rojas (Spain). No weather or pitch problem found.

games.reason: Germany have a clear quality edge (Elo gap about 210, 2-0 win in Munich, Serbia lost 4 of 4 and lack Vlahovic, Pavlovic, Kostic and Stankovic). Market moved further toward Germany since the morning (76.65% to 78.64%) with DraftKings also shortening, and today's expected XI is close to the strongest available. Confidence stays medium because no official XI is out, the right wing and full-backs are open, Germany are blunt in attack (0-0 in Greece), and Serbia are desperate to avoid relegation.
games.main_risk: A draw or narrow Serbian result: Germany scored few goals under Klopp (0-0 in Greece), Serbia face relegation and will press hard, and Klopp could still experiment. Official XI not yet out.

checks.team_news: No new news today. Weiss (head coach since May, no coach-change flag) named 31 players. Out: Lobotka (serious injury, 6-8 weeks), Leo Sauer (muscle injury), Dubravka (meniscus), Obert and Vavro not in the squad; Suslov arrived not fully fit. Back: Rusnak, Bero and Rodak. Skriniar, Valjent, Hancko, Satka, Duda, Haraslin and Strelec are in the squad. My re-check today (ESPN summary, Slovak-language search) found no late injury, illness or withdrawal news for either side. No Faroese squad news was found either.
checks.lineups: Still unconfirmed. The ESPN summary (event 401861160, status Scheduled) lists no rosters yet, and no Slovak or Faroese press predicted XI for today's game turned up. The searches only returned the 2 Oct away game (Greif; Valjent, Vavro, Skriniar, Mesik; Suslov, Lobotka, Rigo; Duris, Bozenik, Sauer), which is outdated because Lobotka, Sauer and Vavro are not available. The goalkeeper is not confirmed (Dubravka out, so Greif or Rodak). Duda, Pokorny and Reis were named as options for Lobotka's role. Expect changes from October.
checks.rotation: Unchanged. A draw is enough for promotion, and Weiss said he would rest key players in Astana on 16 Nov if Slovakia win. That is a risk for the next game, not this one. With many newcomers and a thin midfield, some changes are likely, so this is a soft risk until the XI is out.
checks.motivation: Unchanged. Group C3: Slovakia 10 pts, Faroe Islands 4. A point secures first place and promotion, and a win does so outright. Slovakia will play for the win but need only a draw. Faroe are unbeaten (4 draws) and have little to lose.
checks.form: Unchanged from this morning. Slovakia under Weiss: 3W 1D in 4 (the draw was 1-1 away at Faroe on 2 Oct). Faroe: four draws in four group games. Their strikers (Bobcek, Strelec, Bozenik) are in poor form.
checks.h2h: Unchanged. Latest was 1-1 at Torshavn on 2 Oct 2026. Slovakia have never lost to the Faroes in my sources.
checks.odds: Live Polymarket: home 0.7365, draw 0.177, away 0.086, up from 0.7135 / 0.193 / 0.094 this morning (about +2.3 points on Slovakia). DraftKings via ESPN moved from home 1.34 / draw 4.60 / away 8.50 this morning to 1.32 / 4.90 / 8.50 (opening 1.33 / 4.60 / 8.00), de-vigged 0.702 / 0.189 / 0.109. The favourite has shortened and the draw has lengthened, so the move is in the favourite's favour and the sources broadly agree (Polymarket about 3 points above DraftKings). Total goals 2.5. Live leg prices: over 1.5 0.775, Faroe +2.5 handicap 0.745, over 2.5 0.535, btts no 0.565. No Stake or Rainbet prices seen.
checks.models: Unchanged. World Football Elo: Slovakia 1678 v Faroe Islands 1397 (expected score for home 0.90). It is more bullish than the market, but it ignores the Lobotka, Sauer and Dubravka absences and the Faroes' four draws.
checks.venue_weather: Unchanged. Home game at the Kosice arena, natural grass (the Faroes usually play on artificial turf). No weather forecast found. Normal venue.

games.reason: Re-check about 95 minutes before kick-off. Slovakia v Faroe Islands is verified at 19:45 UTC in Kosice, and no hard exclusion applies. Nothing new hurts the favourite today, and the price moved in its favour: Polymarket rose from 0.7135 to 0.7365 and DraftKings shortened to 1.32. Confidence stays medium because no official XI or announced goalkeeper is out yet. Lobotka, Dubravka and Sauer are absent and the replacements are not named. A draw estimate of 0.20 is held a little above the market's 0.177, since the Faroes have drawn all four group games and Slovakia need only a point.
games.main_risk: A draw. The Faroes sit deep with a physical style and have drawn four of four, including 1-1 with Slovakia in October. Slovakia lack Lobotka, Sauer and Dubravka, have strikers in poor form and a new-look midfield, and need only a point. The XI and goalkeeper are not confirmed.

checks.team_news: Re-checked on 13 Nov (about 95 min before the match): no withdrawal, walkover or fitness report found for either player today. The WTA Day 4 preview and later searches carry no injury news for Andreeva or Muchova. Muchova's injury history is unchanged, and her fitness today is unconfirmed rather than known bad.
checks.lineups: Tennis: the official Friday order of play and court are still not confirmed. I could not retrieve an official WTA Friday schedule. Dimers and other previews give about 3:00 pm ET (20:00 UTC) as the first singles match, which matches the listed start. Nothing new today.
checks.rotation: Unchanged from the morning. Andreeva beat Svitolina 6-4 6-0 on Mon 9 Nov and Sabalenka 6-4 6-0 on Wed 11 Nov, short matches that leave her fresh. Muchova lost to Sabalenka 6-7(2) 5-7 on Mon and to Svitolina on Wed. Both had the same rest.
checks.motivation: Per the morning press (Taipei Times, bets.com.au), Andreeva is 2-0 and through to the semifinals, and Muchova is 0-2 and eliminated, so this is a dead rubber for Muchova with only seeding and momentum at stake for Andreeva. The WTA Day 4 preview only gives pre-Wednesday scenarios, so I could not independently confirm the Wednesday results today. Dead-rubber variance remains: Andreeva could ease off or protect herself, and Muchova can swing freely.
checks.form: Unchanged. Andreeva has two dominant wins at the Finals, including 6-0 second sets. Muchova has lost two straight, one of them a tiebreak set.
checks.h2h: Andreeva leads 1-0 (2024 Ningbo semifinal, Muchova retired injured). The sample is limited.
checks.odds: Live Polymarket Andreeva 0.705 (fair 1.42), unchanged from the morning. The refreshed 24h move is 0.695 to 0.705 (+1.4% relative), small and drifting in Andreeva's favour, with no news shock. The morning check showed the earlier climb from 0.62 on 12 Nov. DraftKings via Dimers was Andreeva -261 / Muchova +240 (de-vig about 0.71). Other books were -200/+154 (about 0.63) and -189/+184 (about 0.65), and the Dimers model gives 0.73. The books disagree, and 0.705 is at the top of that range.
checks.models: Tennis Abstract Elo: Andreeva 2041 (hard 1982), Muchova 1984.2 (hard 1935.7). P(Andreeva) is 0.581 overall, 0.566 on hard and 0.574 blended. That is about 13 points below the market, so Elo sees a closer match than the market does. The Dimers model gives 0.73.
checks.venue_weather: Indian Wells, California, outdoor hard court, afternoon start (about 12:00 pm PT). No weather problem reported.

games.reason: Andreeva is in far better form (2-0, qualified, two dominant wins), has the higher Elo, and is priced as a clear favourite by Polymarket and most books (about 0.63-0.73 de-vigged). Muchova is eliminated and has a history of fitness problems, but no fresh injury news turned up today. p is set at 0.68, 2.5 points below the 0.705 market, because Elo (0.574) and the book spread suggest the market is a little high and the dead-rubber risk is real. Confidence stays medium because the order of play is not officially confirmed and Muchova's fitness is unconfirmed.
games.main_risk: Dead rubber: Andreeva is already through and could ease off or protect herself, while the eliminated Muchova (1984 Elo, took Sabalenka to 7-6 7-5) can play freely. Elo implies only about 57%, books disagree (0.63-0.73), and the order of play and Muchova's fitness are unconfirmed.

checks.team_news: No withdrawal or walkover announced for Sabalenka or Svitolina; WTA Day 6 preview lists the match on Friday's order of play. Sabalenka: no injury reports found (Sky Sports, WTA). Svitolina took an 8-minute medical time-out in Wednesday's win over Muchova and said 'I just have to really put my head down and deal with all the small injuries' and that everyone is tired and struggling with something (Sky Sports). Not enough to call her unfit.
checks.lineups: WTA Day 6 order of play (Fri 13 Nov, Indian Wells Tennis Garden): Andreeva v Muchova from 12:00 PT, followed by [2] Sabalenka v [6] Svitolina, then doubles. Our 21:30 UTC start is 13:30 PT, so the match is second on court and the exact start time depends on how long the first match runs (WTA preview gives only the first start time).
checks.rotation: Both played Mon 9 and Wed 11 (each 1-1). Sabalenka lost 4-6 0-6 to Andreeva on Wed, a short match with 23 unforced errors (one match put it at about 1 h); Svitolina came from a set down to beat Muchova 3-6 6-2 6-2 in just under 2 hours, then planned an ice bath and about 48 h of recovery. Svitolina is slightly more worn; Sabalenka had the shorter Wednesday.
checks.motivation: Group 2 after Wed 11 Nov: Andreeva 2-0, already qualified and group winner; Sabalenka 1-1; Svitolina 1-1; Muchova 0-2, eliminated. The Sabalenka v Svitolina winner takes second place and the last semifinal spot, so it is a straight knockout for both. Sabalenka is NOT qualified, so no soft-risk of low motivation and not a dead rubber. Sabalenka has also won 5 straight WTA Finals openers and is 11-0 at the Finals when she wins the first set (WTA).
checks.form: Sabalenka: beat Muchova 7-6(2) 7-5 Mon, lost to Andreeva Wed after leading 3-1 in the first set (Andreeva then won the last 11 games); won Indian Wells in March and the Australian Open semifinal over Svitolina 6-2 6-3 in January 2026. Svitolina: lost 4-6 0-6 to Andreeva Mon (0 of 6 break points converted), then beat Muchova Wed with only 4 unforced errors in the deciding set. Svitolina lost to Sabalenka in the AO semifinal this year.
checks.h2h: Sabalenka leads 6-1 per the WTA preview (another source says 5-1), has won the last 5 meetings and all 3 on hard courts, including 6-2 6-3 in the 2026 Australian Open semifinals. Svitolina's last win was Strasbourg 2020. Sabalenka's power against Svitolina's defensive counter-punching has favoured Sabalenka on hard courts.
checks.odds: No bookmaker price found for this match (entry has no data.odds and searches returned only older matches; for reference, AO 2026 semifinal prices were about Sabalenka -357 to -385 / Svitolina +292 to +310). Polymarket 0.645 Sabalenka, up from 0.63 24h ago (+2.4% relative), a small move toward the favourite. Fair odds 1.55.
checks.models: Tennis Abstract Elo (https://tennisabstract.com/reports/wta_elo_ratings.html): Sabalenka 2158.5 overall / 2136.8 hard; Svitolina 2026.9 / 1966.2. Win probability for Sabalenka: 0.681 overall, 0.728 hard, 0.705 blended hard. The model is about 6 points above the market; I move p only part of the way (0.67) given Sabalenka's heavy loss on Wednesday and the win-or-out pressure.
checks.venue_weather: Indian Wells Tennis Garden, California: outdoor hard court, desert conditions; the tournament's regular venue for this edition, so not an unusual venue. No weather or wind problems found. Evening start (13:30 PT, second match on court), so conditions should be cooler and slower than at midday.

games.reason: Fixture verified: FAGE WTA Finals Group 2 (called Group B in some sources), Fri 13 Nov 2026, Sabalenka v Svitolina, a winner-takes-the-last-semifinal-spot match. No hard exclusion applies: no withdrawal, motivation is high for both, and the venue is the tournament's regular one. Sabalenka is the clear favourite on h2h (6-1, 5 straight wins), hard-court Elo (about 0.70-0.73) and the market (0.645). Confidence is medium rather than high because of her 0-6 second-set collapse on Wednesday, the knockout pressure, Svitolina's improving form, and no independent bookmaker price.
games.main_risk: Sabalenka's unforced-error spiral under pressure, as in Wednesday's 6-4 6-0 loss to Andreeva (she led 3-1 in the first set, then lost 11 straight games), and a win-or-out nerves factor; Svitolina's defensive game can exploit that. Svitolina's minor injuries and fatigue partly offset this. Start time depends on the Andreeva v Muchova match.

checks.team_news: Coach is Xavi Hernandez (appointed 12 Aug 2026, about 3 months ago, so no hard coach-change exclusion; Koeman left after the World Cup). Netherlands: Van Dijk (physical complaint) and Brobbey (small upper-leg muscle tear, out a few weeks) withdrew and were not replaced, so 23 players. Hato out of the squad, and one report also lists Frimpong and Ake out. Gravenberch was first reported out with a heel injury, but vi.nl's pre-match piece lists him as available, so that is conflicting. Frenkie de Jong is back as captain, Malen is back, and Sepp van den Berg is a first call-up (not expected to start). Greece: no confirmed squad news found. An October report lists Vagiannidis out, and Tzolis's injury extent was unclear before the Germany game; nothing for this match. Coach Jovanovic has kept a stable core.
checks.lineups: Predicted Dutch XI, same in meemetoranje.nl and voetbalzone.nl: Verbruggen; Timber, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Maatsen (voetbalzone has Timber at right-back and Van de Ven in the centre); De Jong, Veerman, Reijnders; Summerville, Malen, Gakpo. Meemetoranje counts six changes from the 2-1 win over Serbia. Greece's likely 4-4-2 is based on the October XI: Tzolakis; Saliakas, Retsos, Mavropanos, Tsimikas; Karetsas, Androutsos, Kourbelis, Tzolis; Pavlidis, Ioannidis. No Greek predicted XI for Friday was found. Some Dutch changes are enforced by injury, but the new back line and the missing striker add real uncertainty.
checks.rotation: Netherlands play Friday 13 Nov, then Germany away on Monday 16 Nov, a short turnaround, so some rotation or rest is possible. The Dutch changes in the prediction come from injuries and returning players, not announced rest, and De Jong and Reijnders are expected to start. No hard rotation confirmed. Greece have the same short gap before their own final game.
checks.motivation: Group A2 (Netherlands, Greece, Germany, Serbia). Before this game Netherlands and Greece both have 8 points and +2 goal difference after four games, Germany 5, Serbia 0. The top two go to the quarter-finals, so both are alive and Greece could be content with a draw. The Dutch need the result to avoid depending on the Germany game.
checks.form: Greece are unbeaten, have conceded only 3 goals in 4 games, won their first two Nations League games, and led the Dutch 2-0 at half-time in Thessaloniki. Netherlands won 2-1 at Serbia and drew 2-2 in Greece after trailing 2-0. Under Xavi they have shown first-half defensive fragility. No xG found.
checks.h2h: 1 Oct 2026, Thessaloniki: 2-2 (Greece led 2-0 at half-time through Ioannidis and Masouras; Van Dijk and Reijnders scored late for the Dutch). The Dutch beat Greece 3-0 in Eindhoven (Sept 2023) and won 1-0 in Athens (Oct 2023). Greece score against the Dutch more often than the market's 63.5% anytime-goal price might suggest, but they are low-event overall.
checks.odds: DraftKings via ESPN: home 1.56, draw 4.10, away 5.00 (opening 1.38/4.60/6.00), de-vigged 59.2%/22.4%/18.4%, total 2.5. The price has drifted against the Dutch since opening (1.38 to 1.56), which is a soft negative. Polymarket 24h move: home 0.635 to 0.625 (-1.6%), small. Polymarket p_market 62.3/21.3/16.3. DraftKings is below Polymarket on the home win, so I shade home down to 0.60 and draw up to 0.23.
checks.models: World Football Elo (eloratings.net): Netherlands 1974, Greece 1804, expected score for the Dutch 0.826, which counts a draw as half and is consistent with a win probability near 0.60 and a draw near 0.23. Elo does not capture the absence of Van Dijk and Brobbey.

games.reason: Game verified (Netherlands v Greece, Nations League A Group 2, home leg, 13 Nov 19:45 UTC) with no hard exclusion: no derby, coach appointed 3 months ago, no confirmed heavy rotation, normal venue.
